theorem_title: Original-edge routes with linearly many steps under arbitrarily many independent affine roofs
preamble:
import Mathlib
open scoped BigOperators
set_option autoImplicit false
formal_statement:
theorem Hirsch.independent_affine_roof_original_routes (n k m : ℕ) (C : Finset (Fin n → ℝ))
    (h01 : ∀ x ∈ C, ∀ j : Fin n, x j=0 ∨ x j=1)
    (D : Fin m → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (b : Fin m → ℝ)
    (hbase : convexHull ℝ (C : Set (Fin n → ℝ))={x | ∀ i,D i x ≤ b i})
    (A : Fin k → (Fin n → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ) (c : Fin k → ℝ)
    (hpos : ∀ x ∈ convexHull ℝ (C : Set (Fin n → ℝ)), ∀ j,0<c j+A j x)
    (u v : (Fin n → ℝ) × (Fin k → ℝ)) :
    let Q : Set ((Fin n → ℝ) × (Fin k → ℝ)) :=
      {z | (∀ i,D i z.1 ≤ b i) ∧ ∀ j,0 ≤ z.2 j ∧ z.2 j ≤ c j+A j z.1}
    u ∈ Q.extremePoints ℝ → v ∈ Q.extremePoints ℝ →
    ∃ L : ℕ, L ≤ n+k ∧ L ≤ m+k ∧
      ∃ p : Fin (L+1) → ((Fin n → ℝ) × (Fin k → ℝ)),
        p 0=u ∧ p (Fin.last L)=v ∧ (∀ i,p i ∈ Q.extremePoints ℝ) ∧
        ∀ i : Fin L, p i.castSucc≠p i.succ ∧
          IsExtreme ℝ Q (segment ℝ (p i.castSucc) (p i.succ)) := by sorry
natural_language_statement: Let the same base be the convex hull of a finite family C of 0/1 points in ambient dimension n and the intersection of m original real linear inequalities. Add k independent coordinates with original bounds 0 <= y_j <= c_j + A_j x, with strictly positive affine heights throughout the base. For any two actual extreme points of the resulting ORIGINAL body Q, construct a route through actual extreme points with nondegenerate whole IsExtreme segments in Q. Its length is at most n+k and at most m+k; Q has m+2k displayed original inequalities. The roof count k is unrestricted and may grow with dimension. No vertex labels/catalogue, neighbor graph, rank, base route or cheap residual-route oracle is assumed. Exact base H/hull equality, the 0/1 generator property and strict positivity remain structural hypotheses. Lower-dimensional/nonsimple bases and zero base/fiber dimensions are retained. This is a structural class result, not unrestricted Polynomial Hirsch, a shortestness or all-facet nonrevisiting assertion, a complete graph-isomorphism theorem, or a polynomial-time algorithm.
source: Reuses the exact accepted #322 namespace prefix (973 lines / 41934 bytes), omitting only its old public root and final print commands. New classification, full-face horizontal and vertical edge transport, Hamming fiber routing, lifted base routing and original-row-count argument are included. This is the separate formal positive affine-roof application, not #325's owned arbitrary-exception-count proof, and not #282's particular triangular chain. Classical 0/1 diameter bounds are credited to Naddef; background on deformed products is Sanyal-Ziegler, arXiv:0710.2162. No historical-priority claim.
